name: Cargomatic — admin, carrier, shipper & driver
description: Every portal, end to end. Admin: order booking and the shorthaul wizard, leg management, accessorials, billing, invoicing, payouts, EDI, documents, audit and Unified View. Carrier: pending tasks, shipment actions, complete stop and POD, offers, payments, drivers. Shipper: booking, invoices, accessorial approval. Plus the driver record. Every node carries the selector the Playwright suite uses; every mutating node carries the API call it fires and the GET that confirms it landed.

env.apiPrefixNote: The admin client calls bare /api/... and /admin/api/... . The edge gateway (proxymatic-edge-*) serves them under /mono, so a browser-observed URL is apiPrefix + path. Match on the suffix, not the whole URL.

sources.note: Every node.selector is copied from a page-object constant named in node.source. Changing a selector here does not change the suite — fix the page object and re-sync.
Express route registrations (app.<method>('<path>')). Path params are the monolith's own (:orderId, :jobId).
node.source is mobile:Class.CONST and the value is "<by>=<value>" — the AppiumBy the page object pairs it with, so a generator does not have to guess.
chunk.access.requires cites the guard and the line that calls it. Roles resolve through SessionStore, so a guard that ORs several roles lists them all.

kind.section: A region of a page that groups fields and actions.
kind.modal: A dialog. Children are only reachable while it is open.
kind.field: An input the test writes to.

legend.api.await: The request the action fires. The step is not done until this settles.
legend.api.verify: The read-back that proves it persisted. scope=record re-reads the whole entity; scope=field re-reads one field; scope=collection re-reads the list.
legend.api.capture: JSON Pointers lifted out of the await/verify response into flow variables, referenced elsewhere as {name}.
legend.api.verifyNotApplicable: Why this write has no read-back. Set it only when none exists — it removes the node from the gap count.
legend.attachesTo: This node lives in another chunk's UI (its menu, its page) but belongs to this chunk's story. Open that chunk to see it in context.
legend.api.reads: A POST that queries rather than writes — UV's grid, the change logs, the distance and price quotes. Marked so it is not counted as an unverified write.
legend.dependsOn: What must already have happened for this chunk to run. kind=session: a sign-in. kind=data: another chunk captured a variable this one needs, with `alternatives` when more than one chunk can produce it. kind=seeded: the fixture supplies it; no chunk does.
legend.provides: Flow variables this chunk captures for later chunks.
legend.edges: Narrative order — which chunk a tester reaches next. `dependsOn` is the harder constraint: what must run first. The two differ, e.g. audit follows invoice.details in the story but only needs {orderId} and {jobId}. The four sign-ins are roots: you pick a portal and start there, so nothing is drawn as leading into them.
legend.access: Who can run this chunk. portal is the sign-in it needs; requires lists the role guards the admin client actually checks, each with the file and line that checks it. gated=false means nothing in the code gates it — not that it is open by design.
legend.platform: android marks a chunk whose selectors are Appium locators ("<by>=<value>"), not CSS.
legend.template: The selector carries a {placeholder} the test must substitute before use.
legend.enum: The values the field accepts, taken from the monolith schema named in enumSource rather than from the dropdown — the UI can be behind.
legend.api.confidence: client = this exact method and path appear in an admin-client API util, so the front end really calls it. route-table = the monolith registers the route but no literal call site was found — the client also builds URLs at runtime through CustomersAPIUtils.method(), and the mobile app is not in this monorepo, so this is not evidence of a wrong endpoint, only the absence of proof of the right one.
legend.variant: This chunk only renders for one value of a field on the record under test. field and test say which, guard and source name the code that decides, and renders names what each side draws. A fixture on the wrong side of the switch makes the chunk look broken when it is simply absent.
legend.planned: The v1 branch ends at the legacy shipments list because the page it opens, /shipments/{jobId} (booking_details_page, 273 selectors), is not mapped yet. Until it is, the v1 side of the order flow stops one step short.
legend.transactionSet: The X12 transaction set this step produces — 214 shipment status, 210 invoice, 990 response to load tender, 204 inbound load tender. transactionSource names the code that builds it.

chunks.name: EDI send & resend
chunks.note: EDI in full. Three outbound transaction sets, from apps/monolith/app/services/v2/edi-service.js: 214 for shipment milestones and holds, 210 for invoices, 990 in response to a load tender. 204 is inbound. Configure before sending — a send against a shipper with no SCAC silently no-ops, which looks identical to a send that worked. The resender tool itself has no page object in playwright-automation, so its three tabs are mapped as API only and cannot be driven by the suite as it stands; that is the gap to close if EDI is going to be covered end to end.

nodes.note: This is what decides whether invoice.generate produces one invoice or several.

chunks.name: Carrier profile (admin)
chunks.note: The capability checkboxes here are what decide whether a carrier sees an offer at all — authorized, hazmat, flatbed, dray operator. Flipping one changes the carrier pool for every future shipment, so a test that writes here is not isolated.

requires.gates: Compliance fields on the carrier form

dependsOn.why: {carrierId} is the carrier under test, supplied by the fixture

nodes.name: Bank transfers disabled
nodes.note: If this badge is up, payout.lifecycle settlement will fail for this carrier.

nodes.name: Test user
nodes.note: A carrier flagged test user is excluded from real offer exposure.

nodes.name: Group payout items
nodes.note: Decides whether payout.generate produces one payout or several.

chunks.name: Legs — add, edit, cancel, hub
chunks.note: Every write leg management has. The four modals share field ids (#legType, #totalWeight, #pickupName) but are separate dialogs with separate submits, so a test that finds #legType has not established which one is open — assert the title first. Cancelling is the only one that cannot be undone from the UI.

access.note: Not role-gated. Reachability is decided by the order's leg_management_version, not by a role.

nodes.name: View details
nodes.note: Opens /shipments/{jobId} — the booking details page, not yet mapped.

nodes.name: Email delivery order

api.verifyNotApplicable: Sending is the effect; nothing on the order changes. Confirm in Mandrill, and remember every environment shares one account.

nodes.note: Sends to a real address. Internal recipients only outside production.

nodes.name: Add Leg description
nodes.selector: p:has-text("Add a new leg to the order")

nodes.name: Create equipment
nodes.note: Same endpoint as the Equipment screen — a leg can mint equipment inline.

nodes.name: Cancel Shipment
nodes.note: Irreversible from the UI. Reason type and code are both required and are what the cancellation reporting is built on.

nodes.name: Add Hub
nodes.note: Hubbing splits the leg at a yard, so the leg count changes — assert on the list, not on the leg you started from.

chunks.name: Shipments list
chunks.note: How you find a shipment without an order in hand — reference-number search across both shorthaul and drayage. The page the pagination bug was filed against.

access.note: No role guard on the shipments list.

nodes.name: Sort by column
nodes.note: Template — {column} is the header text.

nodes.name: Pagination info
nodes.note: Reads "showing N of M". Worth asserting M against the row count — a page that says 28 and renders 25 with no control to reach the rest is the bug this page had.

chunks.name: Shipment detail (drayage)
chunks.note: The biggest screen in the product and the one every drayage question ends up on. Shorthaul models the same URL from its own page object (shorthaul.shipment) with a different set of sections, so the two are alternative views of /shipments/{jobId}, not two pages. Stop completion here writes the same records the driver app writes from the phone — the same stop can be closed from either, which is worth knowing before a test asserts on who closed it.

access.note: The page is not gated. Individual controls are: billing status via order.billing, accessorials via accessorials.request, reference numbers by reference-numbers-admin.

nodes.name: Status badge
nodes.selector: h3[data-testid^='h3-'] + div.inline-flex.rounded-full, h3 + div.inline-flex.rounded-full, h3 + span.inline-flex.rounded-full, [data-testid^='badge-status'], [data-testid^='badge-Status'], .inline-flex.items-center.py-0\.5

nodes.name: Action item
nodes.note: Template — the menu label. Clone, hold, email delivery order and the state transitions all live here.

nodes.name: Distance method label
nodes.note: Reads "Routing: <type>, Version: <n>" — set on the shipper profile, and what a distance dispute turns on.

nodes.name: Assign
nodes.note: Assigning a carrier takes the shipment off the marketplace — the offer disappears from the carrier portal and the driver app.

nodes.name: Reference rows
nodes.selector: div.modal-content:has(h4:has-text('Edit Reference Numbers')) table tbody tr

nodes.name: Email delivery order
nodes.selector: .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header strong:has-text('E-mail Delivery Order')), .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header h4.modal-title:has-text('Send Delivery Order'))

nodes.selector: .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header strong:has-text('E-mail Delivery Order')) input.form-control[placeholder='Comma separated emails'], .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header h4.modal-title:has-text('Send Delivery Order')) input.form-control[placeholder='Comma separated emails']

nodes.name: Close
nodes.selector: .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header strong:has-text('E-mail Delivery Order')) button.btn-default:has-text('Close'), .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header h4.modal-title:has-text('Send Delivery Order')) button.secondary-action:has-text('Close')

nodes.name: Send
nodes.selector: .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header strong:has-text('E-mail Delivery Order')) button.btn-primary:has-text('Send'), .modal-content[role='document']:has(.modal-header h4.modal-title:has-text('Send Delivery Order')) button.button-green:has-text('Send')

api.verifyNotApplicable: Sending is the effect. Confirm in Mandrill — all four environments share one account, so use internal recipients.

nodes.name: Save appointment
nodes.note: Changing a confirmed window is what the missing-appointment-confirmations queue in the carrier portal is built on.

nodes.name: Save
nodes.note: The LMV 2 variant of the same modal — different dialog, same endpoint.

nodes.name: Save arrival
nodes.note: Same transition the driver fires from the phone with the Arrived button — a stop can be arrived from either side.

nodes.name: File complete
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Proof of ')) td [data-testid="CircleButton-3758aad1"], div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Proof of ')) td button.text-green-600, div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Proof of ')) td a[target="_blank"][href]

nodes.name: Complete stop
nodes.note: The last stop completing is what makes the shipment billable, so this is the step order.billing waits on.

nodes.name: Upload document
nodes.note: Which documents are required comes from the shipper profile (StopDocumentRequirements), not from the shipment.

nodes.name: Suggestions
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) a.list-group-item, div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) [data-testid='search-box'] a

nodes.selector: div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) a.list-group-item:nth-child(1), div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) [data-testid='search-box'] a:nth-child(1)

nodes.name: Equipment rows
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) table.default-table > tbody[data-testid^='tbody-'], div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) table.default-table > tbody

nodes.name: Equipment row
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) table.default-table > tbody[data-testid^='tbody-'], div[role='dialog']:has(h2:has-text('Stop Equipment')) table.default-table > tbody > tr[data-testid^='tr-']

nodes.name: Open payout
nodes.note: The link from a charge to the payout it was settled on — the join payout.lifecycle questions usually need.

nodes.name: Uploaded by
nodes.note: Says whether the document came from the driver app or from an admin — the two write the same record.

nodes.name: Save equipment types
nodes.note: Equipment types decide which carriers an offer reaches, same as the carrier capability checkboxes on the other side.

nodes.name: Leg type
nodes.note: chassis_split and bobtail are equipment-exempt — see isEquipmentExemptLegType in apps/admin-client-legacy/src/main/js/helpers/legs-helper.js.

nodes.name: Exception exempt
nodes.note: Exempts the shipment from the exception rules in the exceptions workbench.

nodes.name: Save date
nodes.note: Last free date, outgate, empty return — the dates the past-LFD and empty-pickup queues are driven from.

nodes.name: Save hold
nodes.note: A held shipment stops being exposed to carriers, so an offer test that mysteriously finds nothing is worth checking against this banner.

nodes.name: Clone shipment
nodes.note: Creates a second shipment. A test that clones and does not clean up leaves one behind every run.

chunks.name: Shipment charges & accounting
chunks.note: The same screen as drayage.detail, split out because it is a different job: the shipper side is receivable, the carrier side is payable, and the two tables look alike but have different columns — the carrier one carries rate source, status and paid date, the shipper one carries reason and notes. Each row links to the invoice or payout it landed on, which is the join most billing questions need.

dependsOn.why: the charges belong to a shipment

nodes.name: Open invoice
nodes.note: Charge to invoice. The reverse of the payout link on the carrier side.

nodes.name: Value required
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog'][data-state='open']:has(h2:has-text('Adjust Drayage Accessorial')) span.text-red-500:has-text('Shipper Cost cannot be empty')

nodes.name: Reason required
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog'][data-state='open']:has(h2:has-text('Adjust Drayage Accessorial')) span.text-red-500:has-text('Reason Code is required')

nodes.name: Note required
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog'][data-state='open']:has(h2:has-text('Adjust Drayage Accessorial')) span.text-red-500:has-text('Notes cannot be empty')

nodes.name: Rate source
nodes.note: Says which lane rate or tariff produced the cost — the first thing to check when a rerate changes a number.

nodes.name: Validation error
nodes.selector: div[role='dialog'][data-state='open']:has(h2:has-text('Adjust Drayage Accessorial')) div.bg-red-50 .text-red-700 li, div[role='dialog'][data-state='open']:has(h2:has-text('Adjust Drayage Accessorial')) div.bg-red-50 .text-red-700, div[role='dialog'][data-state='open']:has(h2:has-text('Adjust Drayage Accessorial')) div.text-danger

nodes.name: Save adjustment
nodes.note: FSC is adjusted separately from the base cost — two amounts, two reasons, one save.

nodes.name: Invoice grouping badge
nodes.note: Set on the shipper profile. Decides whether generating produces one invoice for the order or one per shipment.

nodes.name: Legacy variant
nodes.note: Two implementations of this dialog ship side by side — assert which one is open before clicking, the buttons are not the same elements.

nodes.name: Title
nodes.selector: div[role="dialog"][data-state="open"]:has(h2:has-text("Generate Invoice")) h2:has-text("Generate Invoice"), div.modal-content[role="document"]:has(h4:has-text("Generate Invoice")) h4:has-text("Generate Invoice")

nodes.name: Generate without delivery
nodes.note: Creates the invoice but does not send it — the distinction that makes "was it sent" a separate question from "does it exist".

nodes.name: Generate payout
nodes.note: Grouping comes from the carrier profile, the same way invoice grouping comes from the shipper.

chunks.name: Tariffs
chunks.note: A tariff is the priced fallback a lane rate lands on when no specific rate matches, scoped by market, service type and an effective window. Overlapping windows on the same market are rejected by the editor rather than the API, so the validation error is the thing to assert. Node ids keep the pr. prefix they had inside pricing so existing references do not break.

access.note: The nav link is not gated — anyone can reach /tools/tariffs; the write path is what checks, in TariffAPIUtils rather than in the component.

dependsOn.why: a tariff is scoped to a market unless All Markets is ticked

nodes.name: Default
nodes.note: Only one tariff per type should be default. Two defaults is a data bug that prices unpredictably.

api.note: Rates within a tariff are /api/1/tariffRates. Usage across shippers is /api/2/tariffs/usage — check that before editing a live tariff.

nodes.name: No results
nodes.selector: div[data-testid="tariffs"] table.w-full.caption-bottom :is(td, div):has-text("No results"), div[data-testid="tariffs"] table.w-full.caption-bottom :is(td, div):has-text("No data")
